title: Operadic relative zeroth-horn extension from the first correspondence
statement: Use symmetric operadic families, their family maps on simplicial subsets, and the colorwise relative operadic left Kan condition of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. Let $m\geq2$, let $\pi:N^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$ be a small symmetric operadic family, and write $N_K^\otimes=N^\otimes\times_{\Delta^m}K$. Let $q:E^\otimes\to O^\otimes$ be a cocartesian fibration and a map of symmetric infinity-operads. Fix a family map $g:N^\otimes\to O^\otimes$, and a family map $f_0:N_{\Lambda_0^m}^\otimes\to E^\otimes$ with $qf_0=g|_{N_{\Lambda_0^m}^\otimes}$ exactly. Suppose the restriction of $f_0$ to the correspondence $N_{\Delta^{\{0,1\}}}^\otimes$ satisfies the colorwise relative operadic left Kan condition. Then there exists a family map $f:N^\otimes\to E^\otimes$ such that $qf=g$ and $f|_{N_{\Lambda_0^m}^\otimes}=f_0$ exactly. No presentability, additional colimits, terminal active slices, or condition on any later edge is required.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3(B), printed p.330; colorwise mapping-space formulation by Definition 3.1.1.2, Remark 3.1.1.5 Proposition 3.1.1.8 (finite amalgamation, printed p.321), and the output Segal decompositions. Only the special case of a cocartesian q is stated September 18, 2017 edition read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical operadic assertion.

proof.text: Write $M=N^\otimes$, $M_0=M\times_{\Delta^m}\{0\}$, and $M_+=M\times_{\Delta^m}\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}$. We construct compatible simplicial lifts over the fixed $g$, without changing their restriction to the horn. The map $q$ lifts every injective categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration]. Pushouts of such monomorphisms again have this lifting property: restrict a lifting square to the original map, take its lift, and glue along the common domain. The property is also preserved by transfinite composition (successor lifting, compatible union at limits). These operations are permissible cofibrations in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Every inert edge of $M$ has constant $\Delta^m$-coordinate, since an equivalence in the ordered simplex is constant. All vertex fibers are contained in $\Lambda_0^m$ for $m\geq2$. Consequently any simplicial extension over $g$ automatically preserves inert edges, and is a family map by [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family].

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3(B), p.330; proof, pp.334-335. Exact lifting and the inert-edge reduction. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text: We will also use the following consequence of the already cited ordinary cone calculus; it is an argument, not a new operadic existence assumption. For an inner fibration $p:C\to D$, a fixed diagram $u:K\to C$, and a relative colimit cocone $c$, the induced functor $C_{u/}\to D_{pu/}$ is an inner fibration. Indeed [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] with $K_0=\varnothing$ factors it as a left fibration to $C\times_D D_{pu/}$ followed by the pullback of $p$. Its mapping space out of $c$ into a cocone $(z,\beta)$ is the homotopy fiber, at $\beta$, of the postcomposition map from $\operatorname{Map}_C(c(*),z)$ to the space of cocones $u\to\Delta_K z$. This follows from the fixed-boundary mapping formula of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], reversed, and its join-slice comparison [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. The homotopy-pullback square of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] identifies this fiber, relative to every specified base cocone, with the corresponding mapping space in $D_{pu/}$. Homotopy-fiber comparisons are preserved by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], applied to the path-pullback spans, retaining their specified paths. Thus $c$ is relative initial. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]: a map $K\star\partial\Delta^r\to C$ over a specified map $K\star\Delta^r\to D$, whose first vertex cone is $c$, extends for every $r>0$. Opposite reversal of joins and universal cones in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] gives the dual: $\partial\Delta^r\star K\to C$ extends over $\Delta^r\star K$ if its final vertex cone is relative limiting. There is also a direct last-apex variant: $K\star\partial\Delta^r$ extends when its last apex is $p$-final in $C$. Build $K$ by its nondegenerate simplices. At a $d$-simplex the new part has boundary $(\partial\Delta^d\star\Delta^r)\cup(\Delta^d\star\partial\Delta^r)=\partial\Delta^{d+r+1}$. Its last vertex is the same relative-final apex. The dual boundary criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] fills this simplex over its prescribed base; union gives the result. The initial case $K=\varnothing$ is that boundary criterion itself. All these statements fix the full boundary and base, and require $r>0$.

proof.text: For $b$ of coordinate $1$ and arity $s$, choose inert projections $b\to b_i$. In [lem-coef-symmetric-family-active-slice-calculus], $J_b\simeq\prod_iJ_{b_i}$ identifies the canonical cocone to $f_0(b)$ with the concatenation of the canonical cocones to $f_0(b_i)$, including their source diagrams. The colorwise assumption of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] makes each latter cocone operadically $q$-colimiting; [lem-coef-operadic-colimit-finite-amalgamation] makes their product-indexed concatenation operadically $q$-colimiting. The same statement's equivalence invariance transfers this to the actual $J_b$ cone. This includes $s=0$: the empty product is terminal, not empty, and the canonical tuple is empty. We have obtained the first-edge condition at every arity, solely from the stated colorwise condition.

source.place: Proof step (1), pp.336-337, and Proposition 3.1.1.8, p.321. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text:
Here is the base filtration used to build the lift. In $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}$ call a morphism strongly inert if its simplex-coordinate is constant, its pointed map is inert and the injection of nonbasepoint fibers is increasing. Every morphism factors uniquely as strongly inert followed by active: first retain, in their existing order, just those inputs not sent to the basepoint, then apply the original map on those inputs. Call a nondegenerate simplex new if its coordinate image contains every vertex $1,\ldots,m$, and closed if its last arity is $1$. Use semantic names for the following matching (the printed proof interchanges some group numbers). A closed all-active chain is an active seed. A chain with a neutral arrow has a partner obtained by replacing its last neutral arrow before its final active-then-strongly-inert suffix by its strongly-inert/active factorization; deleting the inserted vertex recovers the chain. More generally these paired chains allow an arbitrary prefix: the longer partner has a distinguished strongly inert arrow followed by a nonempty active block and then a strongly inert tail. Finally an open active-then-strongly-inert chain is paired with the closed chains obtained by appending each of its final color projections. A final arity $s$ gives exactly $s$ such output partners. Closed all-active chains are seeds; an open chain of final arity zero has no partner and is a nullary seed. To check exhaustion, read a chain backwards through its final strongly inert block and then its preceding active block. If nothing remains it is an active seed or an output chain. Otherwise its next arrow is neutral (the shorter member of the neutral pair) or strongly inert followed by a nonempty active block (the longer member). The increasing choice makes factorization and the neutral matching unique.
For $k\geq0$, let $F_k$ be generated by the old boundary $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\partial\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}$, all simplices of dimension $<k$, and the $k$-dimensional longer partners of both kinds. In the full base allow any initial coordinate-zero block whose remaining block lies in $F_k$, and pull this subset back to $M$, obtaining $M(k)$. Since $m\geq2$, no new zero-dimensional simplex occurs. Thus $M(0)=M_{\Lambda_0^m}$, the $M(k)$ are increasing, and their union is $M$. It remains to extend a lift from $M(k-1)$ to $M(k)$ for $k>0$.

source.place: Proof, pp.334-335, finite-pointed-map matching and skeletal filtration. Explicit agent combinatorics; group labels replaced by semantic names. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text: First adjoin the active seeds whose nondegenerate base image has dimension $k-1$. Well-order their actual lifted nondegenerate simplices $\tau:\Delta^r\to M_+$ by nondecreasing actual dimension. At each stage put $X=M_0\times_M M_{/\tau}$. The initial-zero-block description and [lem-coef-quasicategory-simplex-join-attachment] express the actual attachment as a categorical trivial cofibration after adjoining $X\star\Delta^r$ along $X\star\partial\Delta^r$; all previously attached simplices stay fixed. Indeed its proper positive-block faces lie in lower base dimension or earlier actual dimension; its zero-block faces are precisely the join-slice evaluation. To fill the model join, take the active subcategory $X_a$. By [lem-coef-symmetric-family-active-slice-calculus], $X_a\hookrightarrow X$ has a left adjoint, so [lem-coef-cofinal-relative-join-slice-restriction] permits a lift on $X_a\star\Delta^r$ to be extended to $X\star\Delta^r$ while fixing its entire boundary. Restriction of the active join slice to $b=\tau(0)$ is a trivial Kan fibration over the source by [lem-coef-initial-poset-slice-restriction], applied to $[r]$, its least vertex $0$, the quasicategory $M_{\mathrm{act}}$, and its full coordinate-zero subcategory. It lifts all monomorphisms by that statement, hence is a trivial Joyal fibration by the weak factorization system of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. It is therefore a functor equivalence by [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations]. The canonical first cone on $X_a$ is the pullback of the cone on $J_b$. Here $b$ has coordinate $1$, since the seed is new, so step 3 and the invariance in [lem-coef-operadic-colimit-finite-amalgamation] make that cone operadically $q$-colimiting. The final vertex of $\tau$ has arity $1$. Therefore [lem-coef-operadic-colimit-active-join-boundary] fills the active join exactly. Its hypothesis $r>0$ holds because a new simplex projects onto all $m\geq2$ positive-coordinate vertices. Use cofinal restriction to fill the full join, then [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration] to extend across the comparison into the actual attachment. Repeating and taking unions fills all active seeds.

source.place: Proof step (1), pp.335-337. The initial-vertex restriction is supplied by the existing general slice lemma. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Next adjoin the nullary seeds of base dimension $k-1$, again ordering actual simplices by dimension and using $X=M_0\times_M M_{/\tau}$. The same comparison of [lem-coef-quasicategory-simplex-join-attachment] reduces to $X\star\partial\Delta^r\subset X\star\Delta^r$, with $r>0$. The final object $v$ of $f(\tau)$ has arity zero. The nullary mapping square in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], for both $E^\otimes$ and $O^\otimes$, says that $\operatorname{Map}_{E}(z,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_{N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)}(\bar z,\langle0\rangle)$ and its $O$ counterpart are equivalences: the two empty products are points. Their composites agree because $q$ is over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. Two-out-of-three, or [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] with the empty-product square, gives $\operatorname{Map}_{E}(z,v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{O}(qz,qv)$ for every $z$. Hence $v$ is $q$-final. The last-apex version of step 2 fills the join. [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration] extends across the comparison. This handles all zero-output chains without demanding a missing color projection or an additional colimit.

source.place: Proof step (2), pp.337-338; nullary case expanded from the empty-output Segal square. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text: The remaining attachments are matched pairs with shorter member of base dimension $k-1$. Order them by the lexicographic rank $(u,v,c,w)$ of a longer member: $u$ counts neutral arrows, $v$ counts active arrows, $c=0$ for closed and $1$ for open, and $w$ counts pairs (an earlier active arrow, a later strongly inert arrow). For an output pair these numbers do not depend on the chosen output projection. Refine ties by a well-order. All faces other than the matched face are already present or belong to an earlier pair. Here is the face check: deleting a vertex reduces dimension and is old unless that face is itself a shorter member not yet matched. For such a face, compose the two adjacent arrows and factor the composite in increasing inert-active normal form. If a neutral arrow is removed or absorbed, the new longer member has smaller $u$. If this count is unchanged but active arrows are absorbed, it has smaller $v$. The remaining cases only move an active factor past a strongly inert factor; if the new final object has arity one while the old one did not, its $c$ is smaller, and otherwise the moved factor removes a counted active/inert inversion so $w$ is smaller. Deleting the very last output vertex is exactly the exceptional matched face; deleting the factorization vertex is exactly the exceptional neutral face. Endpoint deletions not of these two forms either lose a positive-coordinate vertex, hence are on the old boundary, or remove an arrow and fall into the preceding rank cases. These checks also show that proper faces of the shorter member are old. Thus at each successor stage the only unknown faces are the shorter member and its longer partner(s). Their domains intersect earlier domains along precisely these known faces. This provides an actual simplicial filtration, not independent choices of fillers on overlapping horns.

source.place: Proof step (3), pp.338-339: rank ordering and its face check, with the inert-active factorization made explicit. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text:
For a neutral pair let $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^{\{1,\ldots,m\}}$ be its longer chain, with matched face obtained by deleting vertex $j$, $0<j<k$. Pull back the family along $\sigma$. In this pullback every object at vertex $j-1$ admits a cocartesian lift of the strongly inert edge to $j$, by [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. The pullback is an inner fibration of quasicategories (pull back inner-horn lifting), so [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-inner-horn-comparison] makes the preimage of $\Lambda_j^k$ categorically equivalent to the preimage of $\Delta^k$. The same remains true with any initial zero-block simplicial set $Y$ attached before the chain. To see this without assuming that equivalences survive arbitrary pullback, construct $Y$ by its nondegenerate simplices. The case $Y=\varnothing$ is the preceding application. At a $d$-simplex attachment the new comparison is the preimage, over $\Delta^d\star\Delta^k=\Delta^{d+k+1}$, of the union
$$(\partial\Delta^d\star\Delta^k)\cup(\Delta^d\star\Lambda_j^k)=\Lambda_{d+1+j}^{d+k+1}.$$
The omitted index remains strictly inner, and the edge immediately before it is the same strongly inert edge. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-inner-horn-comparison] again. Pushout and compatible union of these injective categorical equivalences preserve lifting against $q$, as in step 1 using [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Hence [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration] fills the whole neutral-pair attachment exactly over $g$. The rank check ensures its other faces were already fixed. This is where inert cocartesian lifts are used; there is no claim of cocartesian lifts of arbitrary active edges.

source.place: Proof step (3), pp.339-340; Lemma 2.4.4.6 and the explicit simplex-by-simplex initial-block argument. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text:
For an output pair, let $\sigma'$ be the shorter open base simplex, whose last arity is $s>0$. Take all actual nondegenerate simplices $\tau:\Delta^r\to M$ whose positive-coordinate tail maps surjectively onto $\sigma'$, ordered by actual dimension; $\tau$ may include an arbitrary initial coordinate-zero block. One attaches $\tau$ together with its cones to all $s$ final color projections; its boundary and all other faces have been filled by step 7 or an earlier actual dimension. Form the pulled-back family over $\Delta^r\star I$, $I=\{1,\ldots,s\}$. By [lem-coef-symmetric-family-inert-cone-initiality], the extension category is $J=\coprod_{i\in I}J_i$, with initial $t_i$ represented by a cocartesian inert extension of $\tau$. The dual join-slice comparison in [lem-coef-quasicategory-simplex-join-attachment], glued over the already filled faces, reduces the actual attachment to $\partial\Delta^r\star J\subset\Delta^r\star J$. Its final-vertex cone is already prescribed, since $r>0$ (a new positive-coordinate simplex must meet all $m\geq2$ vertices). Restrict that cone to the $t_i$. Its edges in $E$ are inert: they lie in the last vertex fiber and are already in the previously constructed domain, whose partial family map preserves the inherited inert edges. For every test object the two output-Segal squares in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] say that these projection cones in $E$ and $O$ are limiting relative to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. Pasting their homotopy pullbacks, with the common lower output-mapping-space diagram, gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_E(z,v)\simeq \left(\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_E(z,v_i)\right)\times^h_{\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_O(qz,qv_i)}\operatorname{Map}_O(qz,qv).$$
This is exactly the $q$-limit test of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test]; the pasting is licensed by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting]. Hence the specified final-vertex cone on $I$ is $q$-limiting. [lem-coef-relative-limit-initial-components] transfers this property to the specified cone on $J$. The dual boundary argument of step 2 now fills $\Delta^r\star J$ exactly, and [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration] fills the join-slice comparison to the actual attachment. Iterate over the actual simplices and over the ordered output pairs. There is no arbitrary relative-limit existence assertion here: the required cone is the already specified inert output cone.

source.place: Proof step (3), pp.340-341: output extension categories, initial objects, relative limits and the dual simplex comparison. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.

proof.text: The active-seed, nullary-seed, neutral-pair and output-pair stages exhaust $M(k)$ by the classification in step 4, so they extend the lift to $M(k)$ from $M(k-1)$. At a limit stage define the map on a simplex using any stage containing it; equality on overlaps makes this independent of the choice and makes every face and degeneracy commute. The same construction at the countable union $\bigcup_kM(k)=M$ yields $f:M\to E^\otimes$. Each individual lift was over the specified $g$ and fixed the previous map, hence $qf=g$ and $f|_{M_{\Lambda_0^m}}=f_0$ are equalities of simplicial maps. By the inert-edge observation in step 1, $f$ is a family map. This proves the assertion using only the first-edge colorwise colimit condition.

source.place: Conclusion of Theorem 3.1.2.3(B), pp.335-341; compatible union and the family-map check. Online source inspected; agent expansion, archive WANTED.
